newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, outlook unclear.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, outlook unclear.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded on Tuesday after a two-session fall and analysts said the roughly balanced buying and selling after price fixing made it unclear how long the market would be able to sustain current gains.
Some analysts said the market mood was good, in part because of the assumption that institutional investors would buy more as the new year begins.

"I don't know if that's true but the market was stable for so long and did not react negatively to news such as the central bank's comment rates might rise...so the market seems pretty strong," said Pawel Hominski of Magnus brokerage.
Other analysts said falls rather than rises were likely.

"There could be a slight continuation of the rises but their scale suggests they're speculative and that there's no fundamental reason for clear upward movement," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.4 percent to 14,342.8 points and turnover rose 12.3 percent to 85.9 million zlotys ($29.9 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 68 to six with nine stocks flat.
The main market had risen 3.4 percent over two sessions and then fell 1.3 percent over two sessions before Tuesday's gain.
Analysts were surprised by the maximum 10-percent rise in moderate trade by top gainer meat processor Farm Food.
They blamed low turnover for the scale of PBR's 9.9- percent surge.
The parallel market's Echo Investment, up 9.8 percent with strong buying after price fixing, extended Monday's surge after it reaffirmed it would sell a subsidiary.
